answer: Split answer. The disposal-review DECISION, once actually taken, is a past fact and belongs in the file's documented history: model it as an E17 Type Assignment (subclass of E13 Attribute Assignment, subclass of E7 Activity) carried out by the records officer (P14 carried out by: E39 Actor), which classifies the file (P41 classified: the file, an E1 CRM Entity) by assigning it a disposition type (P42 assigned: E55 Type, e.g. 'retain permanently' / 'scheduled for destruction'). The reason -- statutory requirement vs curator's judgement of historical importance -- is captured as the activity's motivation (P17 was motivated by: E1 CRM Entity, pointing at an E55 Type value or the statutory instrument). If destruction is actually carried out, that is a further, later E6 Destruction event (P13 destroyed). The RETENTION SCHEDULE and the 'next review date', however, are a different matter: they describe a future action that has not happened yet. CIDOC CRM is explicitly retrospective -- 'CRM is defined to be retrospective and not talk about the future' (Christian-Emil Ore, thread t0483) -- and the SIG itself removed forward-looking activity plans from CRMbase entirely, spinning them out into the separate CRMact extension (Issue 333: 'the sig ... decided to incorporate the models for Activity Plans in the CRMsoc'; Issue 419: 'CRMact will be a stand-alone extension'). So scheduling a future disposal review and its target date is not something the file's CRM-documented history captures -- that is workflow/records-management bookkeeping (or CRMact territory), a different kind of system from what CRMbase models. Martin Doerr's own framing of archival institutions (thread t1306) -- keeping records of another institution's actions completely and in sequence -- fits the retrospective half of this case (documenting that a review happened and why) but does not extend to documenting a schedule of things not yet done.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: E87's scope note ties it to management of an E78 Curated Holding following a curation plan; a single planning-application case file coming up for a one-off statutory disposal review is not documented as part of an ongoing curated holding, and no narrative or thread ties E87 to disposal/retention decisions -- E17 Type Assignment is the direct, evidenced fit for 'assign a disposition to this item'.

rejected_alternatives.option: Modelling the retention schedule / next review date as a CRMbase construct (e.g. an E29 Design or Procedure with a future time-span)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The SIG considered exactly this (proposed class 'Activity Plan' IsA E29 Design or Procedure, Issue 166) and ultimately moved all such future-oriented plan modelling out of CRMbase into the CRMact extension (Issue 419: 'CRMact will be a stand-alone extension'), confirming CRMbase deliberately does not carry future-scheduled actions. Christian-Emil Ore's remark in t0483 that 'CRM is defined to be retrospective and not talk about the future' is the direct statement of the principle.

notes: The tools never returned a hit for the literal phrases 'retention schedule' or 'disposal review' (semantic search returned only loosely related meeting-schedule/deaccession noise) -- the case had to be solved by recognising it as an instance of the general 'future plan vs retrospective record' boundary the SIG argued out in Issues 166/333/419, not by direct keyword retrieval. issues "disposal" surfaced Issue 442 (Curated Holding vs Physical Thing) which looked promising but turned out to be about aggregation identity, not disposition -- a dead end worth flagging.
